primary.text: How does a four-day week affect overtime in small firms in Belgium?
primary.scope: Small firms in Belgium with 10 to 49 employees, 2027 to 2029.
primary.completion_criterion: The question is answered when overtime hours per employee are estimated before and after adoption and the estimate is compared with non-adopting firms.

method.procedure: Match adopting and non-adopting firms on sector and size; estimate overtime hours per employee; test for pre-trends.
validity_conditions: Firms are observed for two years on either side of adoption
limits: The design does not cover firms with fewer than 10 employees

results.claim: Overtime hours per employee fall after adoption, and the fall is larger in firms that shorten the week without cutting pay.
results.falsifier: Overtime hours stay within one standard error of their pre-adoption level in adopting firms and in the matched comparison.
results.evidence_needed: Monthly payroll records for both groups, two years either side of adoption.

warrant.gap_statement: Belgian evidence on working-time experiments reports employee satisfaction but not overtime hours, so the effect on hours worked remains unmeasured.
evidence: A handbook chapter on working-time accounts
